title: Second order-scheduling evaluation: model 2.2 and expanded warehouses (pre-registered 2026-11-07, after the exploratory pass at commit 1496b23)
basis: Hypotheses chosen from the exploratory pass (experiments/orders_v2/exploratory.py, seeds 2000-2009). Tested here on fresh seeds 3000-3019 never run before. The first study (experiments/orders/confirmatory_protocol.json, seeds 1000-1019) and its results are unchanged and separate.
exclusions: advanced warehouse with tight batteries is not tested: in the exploratory pass its runs were dominated by inventory drones stranding (36 Wh packs) and blocking cells or removing the only inspection capability; reported as a limitation.
margins: equivalence margins: C10 and C11 about 5-8% of the exploratory FIFO mean (12.8 and 55.3 orders/1000 ticks), rounded up to 0.5; C12 and C13 +-1.0 (about 1.2% of the base throughput), since the correction should change nothing outside the rare gridlock.
ci_note: percentile bootstrap over seeds (10000 resamples) of paired differences; Bonferroni 1 - 0.05/13

hypotheses.statement: model 2.2, first-study base: NSP completes more orders per 1000 ticks than FIFO (replication of H1)
model 2.2, first-study base: PLB completes more orders than FIFO (the H3 question without the 2.1 gridlock)
basic warehouse, standard order profile (compound and sequenced orders): NSP > FIFO throughput
intermediate warehouse (heterogeneous fleet, role alternatives, joint transport): NSP > FIFO throughput
intermediate warehouse: NSP has a shorter mean order lead time than FIFO
advanced warehouse (3-type crews with a QC stage, forklifts, breakdowns): NSP > FIFO throughput
advanced warehouse: NSP has a shorter mean order lead time than FIFO
intermediate warehouse, large dependency graphs (2-4 lines, 70% chained): NSP > FIFO throughput
intermediate warehouse without role alternatives: NSP > FIFO throughput
advanced warehouse, large dependency graphs: NSP and FIFO throughput equivalent within +-1.0 orders/1000 ticks (the advantage does not carry over)
intermediate warehouse, tight batteries and half the docks: NSP and FIFO throughput equivalent within +-3.0 orders/1000 ticks
first-study base, NSP: model 2.2 and 2.1 throughput equivalent within +-1.0 orders/1000 ticks (the correction does not change behaviour outside the gridlock)
first-study base, PLB: model 2.2 and 2.1 throughput equivalent within +-1.0 orders/1000 ticks
